fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every GCLK register to its power-reset state, except generic clocks and their generators whose CLKCTRL.WRTLOCK reads 1; writing 0 does nothing. The reset takes time to synchronize, and CTRL.SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both clear when it is done.

fields.name: WRTLOCK
fields.text: Writing it locks the generic clock chosen by CLKCTRL.ID, the generator chosen by CLKCTRL.GEN and that generator's division factor against further writes; only a power reset unlocks them. Generator 0 cannot be locked.

values.text: Clock, generator and division factor unlocked.
Clock, generator and division factor locked.

fields.name: CLKEN

fields.name: GEN
fields.text: Generic clock generator that feeds the peripheral clock chosen by CLKCTRL.ID.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Peripheral generic clock to connect to the generator in CLKCTRL.GEN. A power reset returns CLKCTRL to its reset value for every ID, RTC included; a user reset does so for an ID other than the RTC whose WRTLOCK is 0. After a power reset every ID reads GEN 0x00, CLKEN 0, WRTLOCK 0, except WDT (ID 0x03): GEN 0x02, with CLKEN and WRTLOCK following the WDT Enable and WDT Always-On bits of the NVM User Row.

fields.name: DIVSEL

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Generic clock generator to configure or read. A power reset returns GENCTRL to its reset value for every ID, the RTC's generator included. A user reset always returns generator 0 to 0x00010600, and returns any other generator to its reset value unless it feeds a locked generic clock or the RTC clock, in which case it is unchanged. fields.name: DIV

A user reset always returns generator 0 to 0x00000000, and returns any other generator to its reset value unless it feeds a locked generic clock or the RTC clock, in which case it is unchanged. fields.text: Writing 1 turns on the synchronization ready interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Writing 1 turns on the Alarm 0 interrupt by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Interrupt Flag Status and Clear - MODE2

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Goes high one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after the counter overflows, requesting an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.OVF is 1. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Goes high when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless the fall came from an enable or a software reset; requests an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.SYNCRDY is 1. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Goes high one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after CLOCK matches ALARM0, requesting an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.ALARM0 is 1. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: High while registers are being synchronized between the clock domains; goes low when that finishes.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Chooses whether the RTC keeps running in debug mode: 0 halts it, 1 lets it run. A software reset leaves this bit unchanged.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Direction of the frequency correction.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: How much correction is applied to the RTC prescaler; values 1 to 127 adjust the RTC frequency by that amount.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Years counted from a reference year chosen by software; a year whose YEAR[1:0] is 0 counts as a leap year.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Month, 1 for January up to 12 for December.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Day of the month, from 1 up to 28, 29, 30 or 31 by month and year.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Hour. With CTRL.CLKREP at 0 it runs 0 to 23; with CTRL.CLKREP at 1, HOUR[3:0] runs 1 to 12 and HOUR[4] is 0 for AM, 1 for PM.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Minute, 0 to 59.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Second, 0 to 59.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Alarm year; compared only when MASK.SEL is 6.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Alarm month; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 4.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Alarm day; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 3.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Alarm hour; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 2.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Alarm minute; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 1.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Alarm second; compared only when MASK.SEL is above 0.

fields.name: SEL
fields.text: Chooses which parts of Alarm n take part in the match.

fields.name: LVLENx3
fields.text: Lets DMA requests of priority level 3 into the arbiter when 1; requests of that level are ignored when 0. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: LVLENx2
fields.text: Lets DMA requests of priority level 2 into the arbiter when 1; requests of that level are ignored when 0. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: LVLENx1
fields.text: Lets DMA requests of priority level 1 into the arbiter when 1; requests of that level are ignored when 0. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: LVLENx0
fields.text: Lets DMA requests of priority level 0 into the arbiter when 1; requests of that level are ignored when 0. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: CRCENABLE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the CRC calculation on; write 0 to turn it off, which takes effect once CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY is clear. Reads 0 while the CRC is off.

fields.name: DMAENABLE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the DMA module on, 0 to turn it off. A 0 written mid-transfer leaves the bit set until the internal transfer buffer has drained, which happens when the current burst finishes, and the transfer is aborted. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every DMAC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value; only accepted when DMAENABLE and CRCENABLE are both 0, otherwise the request is dropped and the DMAC answers with an access error. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CRCSRC
fields.text: Picks where the CRC input comes from. The choice is locked, and cannot be changed, while a CRC is being computed, until it completes or the CRC module is turned off; CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY shows the lock. With a DMA channel as source, that channel generates and signals CRC completion.

fields.name: CRCPOLY
fields.text: Chooses the CRC polynomial.

fields.name: CRCBEATSIZE
fields.text: Width of each bus access when the CRC is fed from the I/O interface.

fields.name: CRCDATAIN
fields.text: Data to be run through the CRC. The new checksum is ready CRCBEAT+1 clock cycles after a write here.

registers.name: CRCCHKSUM
registers.title: CRC Checksum
notes: Holds the 16- or 32-bit checksum. Resets to zero; writing it directly can set all bits to one, and it can be written only while the CRC module is off. With CRC-32 and CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY clear (CRC done or aborted), it reads back bit-reversed (bit 31 with bit 0, and so on) and complemented; with CRC-16, or while CRCBUSY is set, it reads the raw value.

fields.name: CRCCHKSUM
fields.text: The CRC result. With CRC-16 the upper 16 bits always read 0.

fields.name: CRCZERO
fields.text: Set when a CRC finishes with a checksum of zero; cleared when a new CRC source is chosen. For CRC-32 with the checksum appended little-endian to the data, the final value is 0x2144DF1C, not zero; if the checksum is complemented before being appended, the final value is zero.

fields.name: CRCBUSY
fields.text: Set when a CRC source is chosen and stays set while that source uses the CRC module. With the I/O interface, write 1 to clear it. With a DMA channel, it follows that channel's enable and cannot be cleared by software.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Sets whether the DMAC keeps running while an external debugger halts the CPU. A software reset leaves this bit unchanged.

values.text: DMAC keeps running while the CPU is halted.

registers.name: QOSCTRL
registers.title: Quality of Service Control
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x15.

fields.name: DQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority for data transfers.

fields.name: FQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority for descriptor fetches.

fields.name: WRBQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority for write-backs.

fields.name: SWTRIGn
fields.text: One bit per channel, 11 to 0. Writing 1 issues a software trigger to that channel when its CHSTATUS.PEND is 0; PEND then sets and this bit stays 0. Writing 1 while PEND is already 1 sets the bit. It clears when the channel's CHSTATUS.PEND sets, or when 0 is written to it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN3
fields.text: Selects static or round-robin arbitration among channels of priority level 3.

fields.name: LVLPRI3
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 3 (RRLVLEN3=1), holds the number of the level-3 channel most recently granted access. With static arbitration a non-zero value has no effect on priority. Not cleared when RRLVLEN3 is written to 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN2
fields.text: Selects static or round-robin arbitration among channels of priority level 2.

fields.name: LVLPRI2
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 2 (RRLVLEN2=1), holds the number of the level-2 channel most recently granted access. With static arbitration a non-zero value has no effect on priority. Not cleared when RRLVLEN2 is written to 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN1
fields.text: Selects static or round-robin arbitration among channels of priority level 1.

fields.name: LVLPRI1
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 1 (RRLVLEN1=1), holds the number of the level-1 channel most recently granted access. With static arbitration a non-zero value has no effect on priority. Not cleared when RRLVLEN1 is written to 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN0
fields.text: Selects static or round-robin arbitration among channels of priority level 0.

fields.name: LVLPRI0
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 0 (RRLVLEN0=1), holds the number of the level-0 channel most recently granted access. With static arbitration a non-zero value has no effect on priority. Not cleared when RRLVLEN0 is written to 0.

registers.name: INTPEND
registers.title: Interrupt Pending
notes: Shows the lowest-numbered channel with an interrupt pending.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID is pending.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID is busy.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID has fetched an invalid descriptor.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID has a Suspend interrupt pending; write 1 to clear that channel's Suspend flag. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID has a Transfer Complete interrupt pending; write 1 to clear that channel's Transfer Complete flag. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID has a Transfer Error interrupt pending; write 1 to clear that channel's Transfer Error flag. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Number of the lowest channel with an interrupt pending, valid when SUSP, TCMPL or TERR is set. It updates when a lower-numbered channel gets a pending interrupt or when software clears a channel's interrupt sources, and reads 0 when nothing is pending. Writing it gives indirect access to that channel's interrupt flag register.

fields.name: CHINTn
fields.text: One bit per channel, 11 to 0: set when channel n has an interrupt request pending; cleared when that channel's interrupts are disabled or their sources cleared.

fields.name: BUSYCHn
fields.text: One bit per channel, 11 to 0: set when channel n starts a transfer; cleared when its trigger action completes, on a bus error on it, or when it is disabled.

fields.name: PENDCH
fields.text: One bit per channel, 11 to 0: set while a transfer is pending on channel n; cleared when the trigger action set by CHCTRLB.TRIGACT starts, on a bus error on the channel, or when it is disabled.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit block transfer count of the transfer in progress, kept in the active channel and written back to that channel's write-back location when the arbiter grants another channel. Valid only while ABUSY is 1.

fields.name: ABUSY
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the next descriptor's transfer count is read from write-back memory, and to 0 once the active count has been stored back there.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Index of the channel now held in the active channel registers, updated whenever the arbiter grants a new channel.

fields.name: LVLEXx
fields.text: One bit per priority level, 3 to 0: 1 while some level-x channel trigger request is running or waiting, 0 when there is none.

fields.name: BASEADDR
fields.text: Start address of the descriptor memory section; must be 64-bit aligned.

fields.name: WRBADDR
fields.text: Start address of the write-back memory section; must be 64-bit aligned.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Number of the channel the CH* registers act on. Write it before any read or write of a channel register.

registers.name: CHCTRLA
registers.title: Channel Control A
notes: Acts on the channel selected by CHID.ID.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the channel on. A 0 written mid-transfer leaves the bit set until the internal transfer buffer drains at the end of the current burst, and the transfer is aborted. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return the channel registers to their reset values; only accepted while ENABLE=0, ignored while ENABLE=1. Clears itself when the reset is done. Writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHCTRLB
registers.title: Channel Control B
notes: Acts on the channel selected by CHID.ID.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Software command to the channel: suspend or resume. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: TRIGACT
fields.text: What one trigger starts.

fields.name: TRIGSRC
fields.text: Peripheral trigger that starts the channel's transfers.

fields.name: LVL
fields.text: Arbitration priority level of the channel: 0x0 level 0, 0x1 level 1, 0x2 level 2, 0x3 level 3; a higher level wins over a lower one. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: EVOE
fields.text: Turns on the channel's event output; an event is produced for each condition chosen by the descriptor's BTCTRL.EVOSEL. Present only on the lowest-numbered DMA channels.

fields.name: EVIE
fields.text: Turns on the channel's event input. Present only on the lowest-numbered DMA channels.

values.text: Each incoming event runs the event action.

fields.name: EVACT
fields.text: Action taken on an incoming event, carried out only when EVIE is set. Present only on the lowest-numbered DMA channels.

values.name: TRIG
values.text: Normal transfer; conditional transfer on strobe trigger.

values.name: SSKIP
values.text: Skip the next block suspend action.

registers.name: CHINTENCLR
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Disables interrupts with no read-modify-write; changes show in CHINTENSET too. Acts on the channel selected by CHID.ID.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the Channel Suspend interrupt enable, disabling that interrupt. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the Channel Transfer Complete interrupt enable, disabling that interrupt. Writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Channel Transfer Complete interrupt off. With block action set to none, TCMPL does not set when a block completes.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the Channel Transfer Error interrupt enable, disabling that interrupt. Writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTENSET
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Enables interrupts with no read-modify-write; changes show in CHINTENCLR too. Acts on the channel selected by CHID.ID.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Channel Suspend interrupt enable, enabling that interrupt. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Channel Transfer Complete interrupt enable, enabling that interrupt. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the Channel Transfer Error interrupt enable, enabling that interrupt. Writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTFLAG
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Flag Status and Clear
notes: Acts on the channel selected by CHID.ID.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Set when a block with the suspend block action completes, on a software suspend command, on a suspend event, or when the DMA fetches an invalid descriptor. Write 1 to clear it for this channel; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Set when a block transfer completes with the interrupt block action enabled. Write 1 to clear it for this channel; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Set on a bus error during a beat, or on an invalid descriptor fetch by the DMAC. Write 1 to clear it for this channel; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHSTATUS
registers.title: Channel Status
notes: Acts on the channel selected by CHID.ID.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Set when an invalid descriptor is fetched; cleared by a software resume command.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Set when the channel starts a transfer; cleared when its trigger action completes, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Set as soon as a transfer request arrives and the transfer is pending; cleared when the trigger action set by CHCTRLB.TRIGACT starts, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

registers.name: BTCTRL
registers.title: Block Transfer Control
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number × 0x10.

fields.name: STEPSIZE
fields.text: Address step size, as a multiple of the beat size in bytes; applies to the source or destination address as chosen by STEPSEL.

fields.name: STEPSEL
fields.text: Chooses which address uses STEPSIZE.

fields.name: DSTINC
fields.text: 1 makes the destination address advance during the transfer, by 1 unless STEPSEL=0 gives it a STEPSIZE step; 0 holds it fixed.

fields.name: SRCINC
fields.text: 1 makes the source address advance during the transfer, by 1 unless STEPSEL=1 gives it a STEPSIZE step; 0 holds it fixed.

fields.name: BEATSIZE
fields.text: Size of one beat, a single bus access, for both reads and writes.

fields.name: BLOCKACT
fields.text: What the DMAC does when a block transfer finishes.

values.name: NOACT
values.text: Disable the channel if this was the transaction's last block.

values.name: INT
values.text: Disable the channel if this was the last block, and raise the block interrupt.

values.name: BOTH
values.text: Suspend the channel and raise the block interrupt.

fields.name: EVOSEL
fields.text: When the channel's event output fires.

values.name: BLOCK
values.text: A strobe at the end of each block.

values.name: BEAT
values.text: A strobe at the end of each beat.

fields.name: VALID
fields.text: Marks the descriptor usable. A 0 in descriptor or write-back memory suspends the channel when it fetches that descriptor. Cleared automatically in write-back memory when the channel is aborted, on an error during the block, or when the block completes.

registers.name: BTCNT
registers.title: Block Transfer Count
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number × 0x10.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit block transfer count. The internal counter drops by 1 after each beat and is written to the channel's write-back location when the channel loses priority, is suspended or is disabled (by transfer completion, a transfer error or software).

registers.name: SRCADDR
registers.title: Block Transfer Source Address
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number × 0x10.

fields.name: SRCADDR
fields.text: Source address of the block. With BTCTRL.SRCINC=0 it is the address of the block's last beat. With SRCINC=1 it is SRCADDRSTART + BTCNT·(BEATSIZE+1)·2^STEPSIZE when BTCTRL.STEPSEL=1, and SRCADDRSTART + BTCNT·(BEATSIZE+1) when STEPSEL=0; SRCADDRSTART is the first beat's source address, BTCNT the starting number of beats left, BEATSIZE the bytes per beat setting, STEPSIZE the beats per step.

registers.name: DSTADDR
registers.title: Block Transfer Destination Address
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number × 0x10.

fields.name: DSTADDR
fields.text: Destination address of the block. With BTCTRL.DSTINC=0 it is the address of the block's last beat. With DSTINC=1 it is DSTADDRSTART + BTCNT·(BEATSIZE+1) when BTCTRL.STEPSEL=1, and DSTADDRSTART + BTCNT·(BEATSIZE+1)·2^STEPSIZE when STEPSEL=0; DSTADDRSTART is the first beat's destination address, BTCNT the starting number of beats left, BEATSIZE the bytes per beat setting, STEPSIZE the beats per step.

registers.name: DESCADDR
registers.title: Next Descriptor Address
notes: Offset counts from BASEADDR or WRBADDR plus channel number × 0x10.

fields.name: DESCADDR
fields.text: SRAM address of the next descriptor; must be 64-bit aligned. A value of 0x00000000 ends the transaction when the DMAC goes to load the next descriptor.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the EIC on or off. The change takes effect after synchronization: the written value reads back at once, STATUS.SYNCBUSY sets, and clears when the change is done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every EIC register to its reset value and turn the EIC off; it overrides any other write in the same access. The reset finishes after synchronization, when CTRL.SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: 1 while registers are being synchronized between clock domains; 0 once that is done.

fields.name: NMIFILTEN
fields.text: Non-maskable interrupt filter enable.

fields.name: NMISENSE
fields.text: Edge or level of the NMI pin that triggers the NMI.

registers.name: NMIFLAG
registers.title: Non-Maskable Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: NMI
fields.text: Set, with an interrupt request, when the NMI pin matches the NMISENSE setting. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTEOx
fields.text: One bit per pin, 15 to 0: 1 makes each detection on EXTINTx produce an event.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: One bit per pin, 15 to 0. Writing 1 clears the external interrupt x enable, disabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: One bit per pin, 15 to 0. Writing 1 sets the external interrupt x enable, enabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: One bit per pin, 15 to 0: set when EXTINTx matches its sense setting; an interrupt request follows when EXTINT[x] in INTENCLR/INTENSET is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WAKEUPENx
fields.text: One bit per pin, 15 to 0: lets a match of EXTINTx against its sense setting wake the device from sleep.

values.text: EXTINTx does not wake the device.

fields.name: FILTEN7
fields.text: Filter enable for input 7 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: SENSE7
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers input 7 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: FILTEN6
fields.text: Filter enable for input 6 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: SENSE6
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers input 6 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: FILTEN5
fields.text: Filter enable for input 5 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: SENSE5
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers input 5 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: FILTEN4
fields.text: Filter enable for input 4 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: SENSE4
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers input 4 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: FILTEN3
fields.text: Filter enable for input 3 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: SENSE3
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers input 3 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: FILTEN2
fields.text: Filter enable for input 2 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: SENSE2
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers input 2 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: FILTEN1
fields.text: Filter enable for input 1 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: SENSE1
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers input 1 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: FILTEN0
fields.text: Filter enable for input 0 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: SENSE0
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers input 0 of this register; CONFIG0 covers EXTINT7 to 0, CONFIG1 EXTINT15 to 8.

fields.name: CMDEX
fields.text: Writing the key 0xA5 here runs the command in CMD; the key and CMD must be written together. Any other value is refused and sets STATUS.PROGE, which is also set when an earlier command has not finished. INTFLAG.READY must be 1 when a command is issued. An APB command arriving in the same cycle as an AHB access waits until the NVM block and AHB are idle, the AHB access going first. Bit 0 of CMDEX reads 1 until the command is issued. ADDR.ADDR is a 16-bit (half-word) address.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Selects the command that runs when the CMDEX key is written.

values.name: ER
values.text: Erase Row: erases the main-array row at ADDR.

values.name: WP
values.text: Write Page: copies the page buffer into the page at ADDR.

values.name: EAR
values.text: Erase Auxiliary Row: erases the auxiliary row at ADDR; allowed only on the User Configuration Row and only while the Security bit is clear.

values.name: WAP
values.text: Write Auxiliary Page: copies the page buffer into the page at ADDR; allowed only on the User Configuration Row and only while the Security bit is clear.

values.name: RWWEEER
values.text: RWWEE Erase Row: erases the RWWEE-array row at ADDR.

values.name: RWWEEWP
values.text: RWWEE Write Page: copies the page buffer into the RWWEE-array page at ADDR.

values.name: LR
values.text: Lock Region: locks the region holding the ADDR location.

values.name: UR
values.text: Unlock Region: unlocks the region holding the ADDR location.

values.name: PBC
values.text: Page Buffer Clear: empties the page buffer.

values.name: SSB
values.text: Set Security Bit: turns security on by putting 0x00 in byte 0 of the lockbit row.

values.name: LDR
values.text: Lock Data Region: locks the data region holding the ADDR location; with the security extension enabled, secure regions are locked only by a secure access.

values.name: UDR
values.text: Unlock Data Region: unlocks the data region holding the ADDR location; with the security extension enabled, secure regions are unlocked only by a secure access.

fields.name: CACHEDIS
fields.text: Turns the cache off.

fields.name: READMODE
fields.text: Selects how the NVMCTRL cache system handles reads.

values.name: NO_MISS_PENALTY
values.text: No wait state added on a cache miss; best system performance.

values.name: LOW_POWER
values.text: One wait state added on every cache miss to lower cache power; the CPU stalls on each miss, so run time can grow.

values.name: DETERMINISTIC
values.text: Hits and misses take the same time, set by the programmed Flash wait states, for execution timing that is deterministic in real-time use.

fields.name: SLEEPPRM
fields.text: Sets the NVM power reduction mode used in sleep.

values.name: WAKEUPACCESS
values.text: NVM block goes low-power on entering sleep and leaves it on its first access.

values.name: WAKEUPINSTANT
values.text: NVM block goes low-power on entering sleep and leaves it on leaving sleep.

fields.name: MANW
fields.text: Manual Write; resets to 1.

values.text: A write to the last word of the page buffer starts a write of the page addressed by the last write, memory and auxiliary rows alike.
Writes start only from a command in CTRLA.CMD.

fields.name: RWS
fields.text: Number of wait states on an NVM read, 0 to 15; resets to 0, and software may change it to suit NVM access time and system clock.

fields.name: RWWEEP
fields.text: How many pages the RWW EEPROM Emulation space holds.

fields.name: PSZ
fields.text: Page size; not every device in the family offers every size.

fields.name: NVMP
fields.text: How many pages the NVM main space holds.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the ERROR interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads give the ERROR interrupt enable state.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the READY interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads give the READY interrupt enable state.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the ERROR interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads give the ERROR interrupt enable state.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the READY interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads give the READY interrupt enable state.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Set by an NVME, LOCKE or PROGE error; write 1 to clear.

values.text: No error since the flag was last cleared.
One or more errors since the flag was last cleared.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: NVM Ready.

values.text: Controller busy with a program or erase.
Controller ready for a new command.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Security Bit Status.

fields.name: NVME
fields.text: NVM error flag; write 1 to clear.

values.text: No program or erase error reported by the NVM controller since the last clear.
One or more NVM controller errors since the last clear.

fields.name: LOCKE
fields.text: Lock error flag; write 1 to clear.

values.text: No locked region programmed since the last clear.
A locked region was programmed at least once since the last clear.

fields.name: PROGE
fields.text: Programming error flag; write 1 to clear.

values.text: No bad command or bad key written to the NVM Command register since the last clear.
A bad command, a bad key or both written to the NVM Command register since the last clear.

fields.name: LOAD
fields.text: Set as soon as one or more words are loaded into the NVM page buffer; stays set until a page write or a PBCLR command. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: PRM
fields.text: Shows whether the NVM is in power reduction mode. It enters by command or automatically on sleep, per SLEEPPRM; it leaves by an AHB access to the NVM block, by the SPRM/CPRM commands, or on leaving sleep, per SLEEPPRM.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Half-word offset, from the NVM section's start, used by a command run through CMDEX; also updated by writes to the page buffer. Operation address = section start + 2 x ADDR. To erase the third Flash row (0x00000200-0x000002FF), write any half-word offset in 0x100-0x17F; for the fifth RWWEE row (0x00400400-0x004004FF), any in 0x200-0x27F.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: One lock bit per region, changed only through CMD commands. Erased state is all unlocked (0xFFFF); after reset the bits are loaded from the NVM User Row.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: One bit per pin of the PORT group sets that pin's direction.

fields.name: DIRCLR
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to clear that DIR bit, making the pin an input; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DIRSET
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to set that DIR bit, making the pin an output; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DIRTGL
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to flip that DIR bit, reversing the pin's direction; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OUT
fields.text: For an output pin (per DIR), the level it drives; for an input pin with PINCFG.PULLEN set, whether it pulls up or down.

fields.name: OUTCLR

fields.name: OUTSET
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to set that OUT bit; 0 does nothing. An output pin then drives high; an input pin with pull enabled then pulls up.

values.text: Output driven high, or input pulled up.

fields.name: OUTTGL
fields.text: Write 1 to a bit to flip that OUT bit; 0 does nothing. An output pin's drive level inverts; an input pin with pull enabled swaps its pull direction.

fields.name: IN
fields.text: Each bit reads 1 when the pin's input sampler sees a high level and 0 when it sees a low level.

fields.name: SAMPLING

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Goes to 1 on any error with its own flag in STATUS: SEXTTOUT, LOWTOUT, COLL or BUSERR. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the client has sent or received a byte. Cleared by hardware on a write to DATA, a read of DATA in smart mode, or a valid command in CMD; write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: AMATCH
fields.text: Goes to 1 when a valid matching address is received. Cleared by hardware when CTRLB.CMD is written; write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing. On clearing, ACK or NACK goes out as CTRLB.ACKACT says.

fields.name: PREC
fields.text: Goes to 1 on a STOP during a transfer this client is handling; a STOP between the host and another client sets it only when CTRLB.GCMD=1. Hardware clears it after a command on the next address match; write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the client sees START followed by a host code. Write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing; a STOP also clears it.

fields.name: SEXTTOUT
fields.text: Goes to 1 on a client SCL low extend time-out. Cleared on its own by answering a new START with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD=3) or when INTFLAG.AMATCH clears; write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: Reads 1 while the client holds SCL low to stretch the clock; it follows INTFLAG.DRDY or INTFLAG.AMATCH and clears with that flag. Treat as read-only.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Goes to 1 on an SCL low time-out. Cleared on its own by answering a new START with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD=3) or when INTFLAG.AMATCH clears; write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SR
fields.text: Whether the address match that raised INTFLAG.AMATCH came after a START or a repeated START; valid only while INTFLAG.AMATCH is 1.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Direction of the last address packet from the host.

fields.name: RXNACK
fields.text: Whether the host acknowledged the last data packet sent.

fields.name: COLL
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the client could not send a high data bit or NACK; it then lets go of SDA and SCL and waits for the next packet addressed to it. Meant for SMBus ARP; outside ARP it means a protocol violation, to be handled as a bus error. Raises no interrupt; software checks it to confirm the data went out. Cleared on its own by answering an address match with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD=0x3) or when INTFLAG.AMATCH clears; write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Goes to 1 on an illegal bus condition whoever owns the bus: a START, repeated START or STOP that breaks the protocol (for example START straight into STOP), or a time-out inside a frame. Cleared on its own by answering an address match with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD=0x3) or when INTFLAG.AMATCH clears; write 1 to clear, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Client address the match logic compares against: ADDR[6:0] with 7-bit addressing, ADDR[9:0] when ADDR.TENBITEN=1. A match sets INTFLAG.AMATCH and updates STATUS.DIR to the transfer's direction.

fields.name: GENCEN
fields.text: Answer the general call address: every bit zero, the R/W bit too (a host write).

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Access to the transmit and receive buffers. Reads and writes succeed only while the client holds SCL low (STATUS.CLKHOLD=1), except reading the last byte after a STOP. Each access starts bus activity, which depends on CTRLB.ACKACT, CTRLB.SMEN and the access direction.

fields.name: LOWTOUTEN
fields.text: Turns on the SCL low time-out: when SCL stays low for 25-35 ms the host lets go of its clock hold (if held), finishes the transaction and sends a stop automatically; INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB sets as usual and STATUS.LOWTOUT and STATUS.BUSERR set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: INACTOUT
fields.text: Inactive bus time-out: when on and the bus stays inactive (SCL held low by a host or client) longer than the chosen period, the bus state logic returns to idle. Needed for SMBus, usable without it. Periods assume a 100 kHz baud rate. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SCLSM
fields.text: Picks when SCL is stretched so software can act. Not synchronized.

values.text: Stretch only after the ACK bit.

fields.name: SPEED
fields.text: Bus speed. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SEXTTOEN
fields.text: Turns on the client extend time-out: once SCL has been low for over 25 ms in total between the first START and a STOP, the host drops its clock hold (if held), completes the transaction and sends a STOP by itself; SB or MB sets as usual, CLKHOLD is released, and MEXTTOUT and BUSERR in STATUS set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: MEXTTOEN
fields.text: Turns on the host extend time-out: once SCL has been low for over 10 ms in total within one interval (START to first ACK, between ACKs, or last ACK to STOP), the host drops its clock hold (if held), completes the transaction and sends a STOP by itself; SB or MB sets as usual, CLKHOLD is released, and MEXTTOUT and BUSERR in STATUS set. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SDAHOLD

fields.name: PINOUT

fields.name: ENABLE

fields.name: SWRST

A register write during the reset gives an APB error, and a register read gives its reset value. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST clear when the reset is done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: ACKACT
fields.text: What the host answers after receiving a data byte from the client. It goes out on a write of a command to CTRLB.CMD, or, with Smart mode on (CTRLB.SMEN = 1), on a read of DATA.DATA. Not enable-protected, not write-synchronized.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Writing starts a host operation; strobe bits that always read 0. The acknowledge action applies only in host read; in host write a command gives only a repeated Start or a Stop. ACKACT may be written together with CMD and is updated first. A command is accepted only while INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB is 1. Command 0x1 sends a repeated start and then the address in ADDR.ADDR; to send a different address, write ADDR.ADDR instead. A command sets SYNCBUSY.SYSOP. Not enable-protected.

rows: Acknowledge action, then a repeated Start.

Acknowledge action, then a byte read.

fields.name: QCEN

fields.name: SMEN

fields.name: HSBAUDLOW
fields.text: When non-zero, the SCL low time in High-speed mode: HSBAUDLOW = fGCLK x TLOW - 1. When zero, HSBAUD sets all of TLOW, THIGH, TSU;STA, THD;STA and TSU;STO. TBUF always comes from BAUD.

fields.name: HSBAUD
fields.text: SCL high time in High-speed mode: HSBAUD = fGCLK x THIGH - 1. With HSBAUDLOW at 0 this value also sets TLOW, TSU;STA, THD;STA and TSU;STO. TBUF comes from BAUD.

fields.name: BAUDLOW
fields.text: When non-zero, sets the SCL low time.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Sets the SCL high time when BAUD.BAUDLOW is non-zero; when BAUDLOW is zero, sets both the high and the low time of SCL.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Sets on any error that has a STATUS bit: LENERR, SEXTTOUT, MEXTTOUT, LOWTOUT, ARBLOST or BUSERR. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Sets when a byte is received in host read without arbitration loss or bus error; the host then holds SCL low. Writing ADDR.ADDR, writing DATA.DATA, reading DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or writing a valid CTRLB.CMD releases SCL and clears it, and the transfer waits until one of these happens. Writing 1 also clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MB
fields.text: Sets when a byte is sent in host write, whether or not a bus error or arbitration loss happened; also when arbitration is lost while sending a NACK in host read, or when a Start is issued with the bus state unknown. If arbitration was not lost the host then holds SCL low. Writing ADDR.ADDR, writing DATA.DATA, reading DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or writing a valid CTRLB.CMD releases SCL and clears it, and the transfer waits until one of these happens. Writing 1 also clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: LENERR
fields.text: Sets when a DMA transfer with automatic length gets a NACK from the client before ADDR.LEN bytes are written. Write 1 or write ADDR to clear; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SEXTTOUT
fields.text: Sets on a client SCL low extend time-out. Writing ADDR clears it, as does writing 1, which normal use does not need; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: MEXTTOUT
fields.text: Sets on a host SCL low time-out. Write 1 or write ADDR to clear; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: Sets while the host holds SCL low to stretch the clock; worth reading when INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB has set. Clears after that flag is cleared and a following operation is issued. Writes do nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Sets on an SCL low time-out. Write 1 or write ADDR to clear; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSSTATE
fields.text: Current I2C bus state. From UNKNOWN, writing 0x1 forces IDLE; no other state can be forced. Forcing IDLE sets SYNCBUSY.SYSOP.

values.name: UNKNOWN

values.name: IDLE

fields.name: RXNACK

fields.name: ARBLOST
fields.text: Sets when arbitration is lost while sending a high data bit or a NACK, or during a Start or repeated Start; INTFLAG.MB sets with it. Writing ADDR.ADDR or writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Sets on an illegal bus condition, whoever owns the bus: a Start, repeated Start or Stop that breaks the protocol (a Start followed at once by a Stop, for instance), or a time-out inside a frame. If this host owns the bus, STATUS.ARBLOST and INTFLAG.MB set too. Writing ADDR.ADDR or writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SYSOP

fields.name: TENBITEN

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Selects High-speed mode for this transfer, from repeated START to STOP; may be written in the same access as ADDR.

fields.name: LENEN

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Writing an address starts a transfer that depends on the bus state. UNKNOWN: INTFLAG.MB and STATUS.BUSERR set and nothing more happens. BUSY: the host waits for IDLE. IDLE: the host sends a start and the address; on an ACK it holds SCL low and sets STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB. OWNER: a repeated start follows, preceded by the acknowledge action if the last transfer was a read; this write is made with one of the SB or MB flags of INTFLAG set. The write clears the BUSERR and ARBLOST bits of STATUS and the MB and SB flags of INTFLAG. Reading ADDR never disturbs the bus. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Host transmit and receive buffer. Reads and writes are valid only while the host holds SCL low (STATUS.CLKHOLD set), except reading the last byte after a stop has gone out. An access to DATA.DATA starts bus activity set by CTRLB.ACKACT, CTRLB.SMEN and the access direction. A write always synchronizes; a read synchronizes only in Smart mode.

values.name: HOLD
values.text: Hold IDX: the next cycle repeats the current one.

fields.name: ONESHOT
fields.text: One-shot mode stops the counter at the next overflow or underflow, or on a stop command; a 1 here turns one-shot on, a 0 does nothing.

values.text: Counter stops at the next overflow or underflow.

fields.name: LUPD
fields.text: Lock on hardware updates of the buffered registers; while set, buffer values do not move in on an UPDATE, so every buffer can be loaded before the next update and then unlocked. Does nothing during input capture. A 1 here sets the lock; a 0 does nothing.

values.text: On a hardware update, CCBx, PERB, PGVB, PGOB and SWAPBx load into CCx, PER, PGV, PGO and SWAPx.
On a hardware update, CCBx, PERB, PGVB, PGOB and SWAPBx do not load into CCx, PER, PGV, PGO and SWAPx.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Counting direction; a 1 written here clears the bit so the counter counts up, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CCB
fields.text: Set while CCBx is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done. Present only for the channels this TCC has.

fields.name: PERB
fields.text: Set while PERB is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: WAVEB
fields.text: Set while WAVEB is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: PATTB
fields.text: Set while PATTB is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: CC
fields.text: Set while CCx is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done. Present only for the channels this TCC has.

fields.name: PER
fields.text: Set while PER is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: WAVE
fields.text: Set while WAVE is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: PATT
fields.text: Set while PATT is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Set while COUNT is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: STATUS
fields.text: Set while STATUS is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: CTRLB
fields.text: Set while CTRLB is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set while CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: FILTERVAL
fields.text: Filter length for the MCEx (x = 0, 1) event input; must be zero when MCEx is a synchronous event.

fields.name: BLANKVAL
fields.text: Blanking time: after the chosen waveform edge (FCTRLn.BLANK), the fault input is ignored for BLANKVAL prescaled GCLK_TCC periods.

fields.name: CAPTURE
fields.text: What recoverable Fault n captures and when it raises its interrupt or event.

values.name: CAPT
values.text: On each Fault n rising edge, COUNT is captured into the CHSEL channel; INTFLAG.FAULTn sets on every capture.

values.name: CAPTMIN
values.text: On a Fault n rising edge, COUNT is captured into the CHSEL channel only if below the last stored CC value; INTFLAG.FAULTn sets on each new minimum.

values.name: CAPTMAX
values.text: On a Fault n rising edge, COUNT is captured into the CHSEL channel only if above the last stored CC value; INTFLAG.FAULTn sets on each new maximum.

values.name: LOCMIN
values.text: On each Fault n rising edge, COUNT is captured into the CHSEL channel; INTFLAG.FAULTn sets on each local minimum.

values.name: LOCMAX
values.text: On each Fault n rising edge, COUNT is captured into the CHSEL channel; INTFLAG.FAULTn sets on each local maximum.

values.name: DERIV0
values.text: On each Fault n rising edge, COUNT is captured into the CHSEL channel; INTFLAG.FAULTn sets on each local maximum or minimum.

values.name: CAPTMARK
values.text: Capture with the ramp index as the top bit.

fields.name: CHSEL
fields.text: Channel that receives the capture made on recoverable Fault n.

fields.name: HALT
fields.text: Halt action taken on recoverable Fault n.

fields.name: RESTART
fields.text: Turns on the restart action for Fault n.

fields.name: BLANK
fields.text: Where blanking of recoverable Fault n begins.

values.name: RISE
values.text: Rising edge of the waveform output.

values.name: FALL
values.text: Falling edge of the waveform output.

values.name: BOTH
values.text: Every edge of the waveform output.

fields.name: QUAL
fields.text: Turns on qualification of the recoverable Fault n input.

values.text: Fault input is not masked by the CMPx state.
Fault input is masked while the output is inactive (CMPx = 0).

fields.name: KEEP
fields.text: Turns on the keep action for Fault n.

values.text: Fault n state ends as soon as the fault goes away.
Fault n state ends at the end of the TCC cycle.

fields.name: SRC
fields.text: Event input that drives recoverable Fault n; the event channel feeding MCEx must route it asynchronously for this use.

values.name: ALTFAULT
values.text: The A or B fault state the previous period ended with.

fields.name: DTHS
fields.text: High-side dead time, in GCLK_TCC cycles.

fields.name: DTLS
fields.text: Low-side dead time, in GCLK_TCC cycles.

fields.name: DTIENx
fields.text: Turns on dead-time insertion for output matrix x, which then drives output [x] with the low side and [x+WO_NUM/2] with the high side.

values.text: Outputs [x] and [x+WO_NUM/2] get dead-time insertion from matrix output [x].

fields.name: OTMX
fields.text: Routing of the waveform outputs to the port pins through the output matrix.

fields.name: FILTERVAL1
fields.text: Filter length for the TCE1 event input; must be 0x0 when TCE1 is a synchronous event.

fields.name: FILTERVAL0
fields.text: Filter length for the TCE0 event input; must be 0x0 when TCE0 is a synchronous event.

fields.name: INVENx
fields.text: A 1 inverts output WO[x]; a 0 leaves it uninverted.

fields.name: NRVx
fields.text: Level an overridden output takes during a non-recoverable fault.

fields.name: NREx
fields.text: Lets a non-recoverable fault override output x with its NRVx level.

values.text: Output goes tri-state on a non-recoverable fault.
Output goes to its NRVx level on a non-recoverable fault.

fields.name: FDDBD
fields.text: Raises a fault when the TCC is halted in Debug mode; zero by default, unaffected by software reset, and not to be changed while the TCC is enabled.

values.text: No fault on a debug halt.
A debug halt raises a non-recoverable fault and sets FAULTD.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Keeps the TCC running while the device is halted in Debug mode; unaffected by software reset, and not to be changed while the TCC is enabled.

values.text: TCC stops in a debug halt.
TCC keeps running in a debug halt.

fields.name: MCEOx
fields.text: Turns on the event output for each match or capture on channel x.

values.text: No match/capture event from channel x.
Event on every compare or capture on channel x.

fields.name: MCEIx
fields.text: Turns on the match or capture input event to channel CCx.

fields.name: TCEIx
fields.text: Turns on TCC event input x.

fields.name: TCINVx
fields.text: Inverts TCC event input x.

fields.name: CNTEO
fields.text: Turns on the counter cycle event, given at the start or end of a cycle as CNTSEL sets.

values.text: Counter cycle event given as CNTSEL sets.

fields.name: TRGEO
fields.text: Turns on an event each time the counter retriggers.

fields.name: OVFEO
fields.text: Turns on an event when the counter reaches TOP or ZERO.

values.text: Event on every overflow or underflow.

fields.name: CNTSEL
fields.text: Point in the counter cycle at which the counter event and interrupt are given.

values.name: BOUNDARY
values.text: Start of the first cycle and end of the last.

fields.name: EVACT1
fields.text: Action the TCC takes on the TCE1 event input.

values.name: DIR
values.text: Asynchronous: event sets the count direction.

values.name: PPW
values.text: Period into CC0, pulse width into CC1.

values.name: PWP
values.text: Period into CC1, pulse width into CC0.

fields.name: EVACT0
fields.text: Action the TCC takes on the TCE0 event input.

values.name: COUNT
values.text: Asynchronous: count while the event is active.

registers.name: INTENCLR
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Clear
notes: Writing 1s here disables interrupts without a read-modify-write; the result also shows in INTENSET.

fields.name: MCx
fields.text: A 1 turns off the channel x match/capture interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

values.text: Match or capture channel x interrupt off.
Match or capture channel x interrupt on.

fields.name: FAULT1
fields.text: A 1 disables the non-recoverable fault 1 interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAULT0
fields.text: A 1 disables the non-recoverable fault 0 interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAULTB
fields.text: A 1 disables the recoverable fault B interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAULTA
fields.text: A 1 disables the recoverable fault A interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DFS
fields.text: A 1 disables the debug fault state interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: UFS
fields.text: A 1 disables the non-recoverable update fault interrupt; a 0 does nothing. Present only on variant L devices.

fields.name: ERR
fields.text: A 1 disables the error interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CNT
fields.text: A 1 disables the counter interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TRG
fields.text: A 1 disables the retrigger interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: A 1 disables the overflow interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTENSET
registers.title: Interrupt Enable Set
notes: Writing 1s here enables interrupts without a read-modify-write; the result also shows in INTENCLR.

fields.name: MCx
fields.text: A 1 turns on the channel x match/capture interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

values.text: Match or capture channel x interrupt off.
Match or capture channel x interrupt on.

fields.name: FAULT1
fields.text: A 1 enables the non-recoverable fault 1 interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAULT0
fields.text: A 1 enables the non-recoverable fault 0 interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAULTB
fields.text: A 1 enables the recoverable fault B interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAULTA
fields.text: A 1 enables the recoverable fault A interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DFS
fields.text: A 1 enables the debug fault state interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: UFS
fields.text: A 1 enables the non-recoverable update fault interrupt; a 0 does nothing. Present only on variant L devices.

fields.name: ERR
fields.text: A 1 enables the error interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CNT
fields.text: A 1 enables the counter interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TRG
fields.text: A 1 enables the retrigger interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: A 1 enables the overflow interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MCx
fields.text: Sets one CLK_TCC_COUNT cycle after a compare match, or when CCx holds a new capture; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing, and in capture a read of CCx clears it.

fields.name: FAULT1
fields.text: Sets one CLK_TCC_COUNT cycle after non-recoverable fault 1; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAULT0
fields.text: Non-recoverable fault 0 flag; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAULTB
fields.text: Sets one CLK_TCC_COUNT cycle after recoverable fault B; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FAULTA
fields.text: Recoverable fault A flag, set one CLK_TCC_COUNT cycle after the fault; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DFS
fields.text: Sets one CLK_TCC_COUNT cycle after a debug fault state; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: UFS
fields.text: Sets when the ramp index changes while CTRLBSET.LUPD is set; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing. Present only on variant L devices.

fields.name: ERR
fields.text: Sets when a channel captures again while its MCx flag is still set, leaving the new capture nowhere to go; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CNT
fields.text: Sets on the CLK_TCC_COUNT cycle following a counter event; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TRG
fields.text: Sets one CLK_TCC_COUNT cycle after the counter retriggers; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Sets one CLK_TCC_COUNT cycle after an overflow; a 1 clears it, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Current compare output level of channel x.

fields.name: CCBVx
fields.text: Compare channel: sets when CCBx is written and clears on an UPDATE, or by writing a 1 while CTRLB.LUPD is set. Capture channel: sets when CCBx holds a new capture and clears when CCx is read.

fields.name: FAULTx
fields.text: Set by hardware when non-recoverable fault x occurs; cleared by writing a 1 once FAULTxIN is low. The counter then resumes from its last COUNT, unless a restart command (CTRLBSET.CMD) is given before clearing, which starts it from BOTTOM.

fields.name: FAULTB
fields.text: Set by hardware when recoverable fault B occurs; cleared by hardware when the fault B action resumes, or by writing a 1 while FAULTBIN is low. With a software halt (HALT = SW), clearing it releases the counter.

fields.name: FAULTA
fields.text: Set by hardware when recoverable fault A occurs; cleared by hardware when the fault A action resumes, or by writing a 1 while FAULTAIN is low. With a software halt (HALT = SW), clearing it releases the counter.

fields.name: FAULT1IN
fields.text: Reads 1 while non-recoverable fault 1 input is active.

fields.name: FAULT0IN
fields.text: Reads 1 while non-recoverable fault 0 input is active.

fields.name: FAULTBIN
fields.text: Reads 1 while recoverable fault B input is active.

fields.name: FAULTAIN
fields.text: Reads 1 while recoverable fault A input is active.

fields.name: PERBV
fields.text: Sets when PERB is written; cleared by writing a 1, or by hardware on an UPDATE while the CTRLB.LUPD lock is on.

fields.name: WAVEBV
fields.text: Sets when WAVEB is written; cleared by writing a 1, or by hardware on an UPDATE while the CTRLB.LUPD lock is on.

fields.name: PATTBV
fields.text: Sets when PATTB is written; cleared by writing a 1, or by hardware on an UPDATE while the CTRLB.LUPD lock is on.

fields.name: DFS
fields.text: Set by hardware in Debug mode when DBGCTRL.FDDBD is set; cleared by writing a 1 once out of Debug mode. While set, the counter halts and the outputs follow DRVCTRL.NRE and DRVCTRL.NRV.

fields.name: UFS
fields.text: Hardware sets it if the ramp index moves while CTRLBSET.LUPD is set; writing a 1 clears it. While set, the outputs follow DRVCTRL.NRE and DRVCTRL.NRV.

fields.name: IDX
fields.text: Ramp cycle in RAMP2 and RAMP2A: 0 in cycle A, 1 in cycle B; always 0 in RAMP1.

fields.name: STOP
fields.text: Sets when the TCC halts, either from a STOP command or from an UPDATE in one-shot mode (CTRLBSET.ONESHOT = 1); clears at the next count up or down.

registers.name: COUNT
registers.title: Counter Value
notes: Before reading COUNT, write CTRLBSET.CMD = READSYNC to synchronize it.

fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Counter value. In 16-bit mode the unused upper bits read 0. The field's low bit m follows CTRLA.RESOLUTION: bit 0 for NONE, 4 for DITH4, 5 for DITH5, 6 for DITH6.

fields.name: PGV
fields.text: Level each waveform output takes under pattern generation.

fields.name: PGE
fields.text: A 1 makes a waveform output take its PGVn level in place of the SWAP output.

fields.name: SWAP
fields.text: A 1 swaps DTI outputs [x] and [x+WO_NUM/2]; DTIxEN does not change the swap.

fields.name: POL
fields.text: Output polarity of channel x in single-slope and dual-slope PWM.

values.text: Output starts at ~DIR, goes to DIR on a CCx match.
Output starts at DIR, goes to ~DIR on a CCx match.
Output goes to ~DIR on a CCx match.
Output goes to DIR on a CCx match.

fields.name: CICCEN
fields.text: Turns on the circular compare buffer for channel x: on an UPDATE, the CCx value is copied back.

fields.name: CIPEREN
fields.text: Turns on the circular period buffer: on an UPDATE, PER is copied back into PERB.

fields.name: RAMP
fields.text: Ramp mode; not synchronized.

values.name: RAMP2C
values.text: Critical RAMP2; variant L devices only.

fields.name: WAVEGEN
fields.text: Waveform mode, which sets TOP and whether a frequency or a PWM wave is made; not synchronized. 0x0 NFRQ normal frequency: TOP = PER, update at TOP/ZERO, output toggles on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down. 0x1 MFRQ match frequency: as NFRQ but TOP = CC0. 0x2 NPWM normal PWM: TOP = PER, update at TOP/ZERO, output set on match and cleared on update, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down. 0x3 reserved. 0x4 DSCRITICAL and 0x5 DSBOTTOM dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at ZERO. 0x6 DSBOTH dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at TOP and ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at TOP and ZERO. 0x7 DSTOP dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at TOP.

values.name: NFRQ
values.text: Normal frequency: TOP = PER, update at TOP/ZERO, output toggles on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.

values.name: MFRQ
values.text: Match frequency: TOP = CC0, update at TOP/ZERO, output toggles on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.

values.name: NPWM
values.text: Normal PWM: TOP = PER, update at TOP/ZERO, output set on match and cleared on update, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.

values.name: DSCRITICAL
values.text: Dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at ZERO counting down.

values.name: DSBOTTOM
values.text: Dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at ZERO counting down.

values.name: DSBOTH
values.text: Dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at TOP and ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.

values.name: DSTOP
values.text: Dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at TOP counting up.

registers.name: PER
registers.title: Period Value
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xFFFFFFFF.

fields.name: PER
fields.text: Period value. In 16-bit mode the unused upper bits read 0. The field's low bit m follows CTRLA.RESOLUTION: bit 0 for NONE, 4 for DITH4, 5 for DITH5, 6 for DITH6.

fields.name: DITHER
fields.text: Extra cycles added to the PWM period every 64 PWM frames. The low n bits, n set by CTRLA.RESOLUTION: none for NONE, 3:0 for DITH4, 4:0 for DITH5, 5:0 for DITH6.

registers.name: CC
registers.title: Compare/Capture Channel x
notes: CCx is a 16- or 24-bit value. In capture it is the second buffer stage and the CPU/DMA access point; in compare it is matched against the counter, normally to make the waveform. It loads from CCBx on an UPDATE, and in match frequency mode CC0 sets the period.

fields.name: CC
fields.text: Compare or capture value of channel x. In 16-bit mode the unused upper bits read 0. The field's low bit m follows CTRLA.RESOLUTION: bit 0 for NONE, 4 for DITH4, 5 for DITH5, 6 for DITH6.

fields.name: DITHER
fields.text: Extra cycles added to the PWM pulse width every 64 PWM frames. The low n bits, n set by CTRLA.RESOLUTION: none for NONE, 3:0 for DITH4, 4:0 for DITH5, 5:0 for DITH6.

fields.name: PGVB
fields.text: Buffer for PGV; with double buffering, a valid value moves into PGV on an UPDATE.

fields.name: PGEB
fields.text: Buffer for PGE; with double buffering, a valid value moves into PGE on an UPDATE.

fields.name: SWAPB
fields.text: Buffer for SWAP; with double buffering, valid bits move into SWAPx on an UPDATE.

fields.name: POLB
fields.text: Buffer for POL; with double buffering, valid bits move into POLx on an UPDATE.

fields.name: CICCENB
fields.text: Buffer for CICCEN; with double buffering, valid bits move into CICCENx on an UPDATE.

fields.name: CIPERENB
fields.text: Buffer for CIPEREN; with double buffering, a valid bit moves into CIPEREN on an UPDATE.

fields.name: RAMPB
fields.text: Buffer for RAMP; with double buffering, valid bits move into RAMP on an UPDATE.

values.name: RAMP2C
values.text: Critical RAMP2; variant L devices only.

fields.name: WAVEGENB
fields.text: Buffer for WAVEGEN; with double buffering, valid bits move into WAVEGEN on an UPDATE. Codes as WAVEGEN: 0x0 NFRQ, 0x1 MFRQ, 0x2 NPWM, 0x3 reserved, 0x4 DSCRITICAL, 0x5 DSBOTTOM, 0x6 DSBOTH, 0x7 DSTOP.

values.name: NFRQ
values.text: Normal frequency: TOP = PER, update at TOP/ZERO, output toggles on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.

values.name: MFRQ
values.text: Match frequency: TOP = CC0, update at TOP/ZERO, output toggles on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.

values.name: NPWM
values.text: Normal PWM: TOP = PER, update at TOP/ZERO, output set on match and cleared on update, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.

values.name: DSCRITICAL
values.text: Dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at ZERO counting down.

values.name: DSBOTTOM
values.text: Dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at ZERO counting down.

values.name: DSBOTH
values.text: Dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at TOP and ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at TOP up and ZERO down.

values.name: DSTOP
values.text: Dual-slope PWM: TOP = PER, update at ZERO, output to ~DIR on match, overflow at TOP counting up.

registers.name: PERB
registers.title: Period Buffer Value
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xFFFFFFFF.

fields.name: PERB
fields.text: Period buffer; moves into PER on an UPDATE. In 16-bit mode the unused upper bits read 0. The field's low bit m follows CTRLA.RESOLUTION: bit 0 for NONE, 4 for DITH4, 5 for DITH5, 6 for DITH6.

fields.name: DITHERB
fields.text: Buffer for PER.DITHER; with double buffering, moves into PER.DITHER on an UPDATE. The low n bits, n set by CTRLA.RESOLUTION: none for NONE, 3:0 for DITH4, 4:0 for DITH5, 5:0 for DITH6.

registers.name: CCB
registers.title: Channel x Compare/Capture Buffer Value
notes: CCBx loads into CCx on a TCC update.

fields.name: CCB
fields.text: Compare/capture buffer for CCx; a CPU or DMA access to it changes STATUS.CCBVx. In 16-bit mode the unused upper bits read 0. The field's low bit m follows CTRLA.RESOLUTION: bit 0 for NONE, 4 for DITH4, 5 for DITH5, 6 for DITH6.

fields.name: DITHERB
fields.text: Buffer for CCx.DITHER; with double buffering, moves into CCx.DITHER on an UPDATE. The low n bits, n set by CTRLA.RESOLUTION: none for NONE, 3:0 for DITH4, 4:0 for DITH5, 5:0 for DITH6.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Picks USB device or host operation.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps the USB clock running in standby; enable-protected.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the USB on or off; write-synchronized. The written value reads back at once while SYNCBUSY.ENABLE stays set until the change has taken effect.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A 1 returns every USB register to reset and disables the USB, overriding any other write in the same access; a 0 does nothing. Write-synchronized; CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST clear once the reset finishes.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set while ENABLE is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while SWRST is being synchronized across clock domains; clears when that is done.

registers.name: QOSCTRL
registers.title: QOS Control
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x000x0F.

fields.name: DQOS
fields.text: SRAM access priority for endpoint or pipe data reads and writes.

fields.name: CQOS
fields.text: SRAM access priority for endpoint or pipe configuration reads and writes.

registers.name: FSMSTATUS
registers.title: Finite State Machine Status
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xXXXX.

fields.name: FSMSTATE
fields.text: Current state of the USB controller's state machine.

values.name: OFF
values.text: L3: powered off, disconnected and disabled.

fields.name: DESCADD
fields.text: RAM base address of the main USB descriptor; the two lowest bits must be 0.

registers.name: PADCAL
registers.title: Pad Calibration
notes: Before the USB is enabled, software must load PADCAL with the pad trim values stored in the NVM software calibration area, or the specified accuracy is not met.

fields.name: TRIM
fields.text: Trims the rise/fall matching of DP and DM.

fields.name: TRANSN
fields.text: Trims the NMOS output impedance of the DP/DM drivers.

fields.name: TRANSP
fields.text: Trims the PMOS output impedance of the DP/DM drivers.

fields.name: LPMHDSK
fields.text: Chooses how the device answers a Link Power Management transaction.

fields.name: GNAK
fields.text: Sets how NAK is used. Not synchronized.

values.text: The handshake reflects the outcome of the USB transaction.
Every USB transaction gets a NAK, whatever the state of the endpoint's memory bank.

fields.name: OPMODE2
fields.text: Specific operational mode of the UTMI transceiver.

values.text: Test mode with bit stuffing and NRZI encoding turned off.

fields.name: NREPLY
fields.text: Applies to endpoint 0 only; hardware clears it when a SETUP packet arrives.

values.text: NO_REPLY off: endpoint 0 transactions follow USB 2.0.
NO_REPLY on: every endpoint 0 transaction except SETUP is ignored.

fields.name: SPDCONF
fields.text: Picks the device speed.

values.text: High-speed test mode (HSTM): high speed forced for test.

fields.name: UPRSM
fields.text: Requests a remote-wakeup resume to the host; cleared when the resume has gone out or a USB reset arrives.

values.text: Writing 1 sends an upstream resume to the host for remote wakeup.

fields.name: DETACH
fields.text: Detach.

values.text: Device attached to the bus; traffic can flow.
Default at reset: internal pull-ups off, which takes the device off the bus.

fields.name: ADDEN
fields.text: Turns the programmed device address on or off; a USB reset clears it.

values.text: Writing 0 turns the DADD address off; the device goes back to address 0.
Writing 1 puts the DADD address in use.

fields.name: DADD
